answer: An applicant takes a single marble gauge post in a delta distributary, locking a 60-credit bond. It releases a violet dye pulse and files its arrival time; an auditor recomputes flow from the public delta flow table, and a mismatch over 3% burns the bond. Filing starts at 42 credits; the kth costs 42+5(k-1), since each new post needs a farther survey, with no reuse, so the 1000th costs 5037 and 1000 fakes pay 2,539,500 plus 60,000 locked. A rented-post ring fails: one post yields one timed pulse per epoch, and a duplicate serial forfeits both bonds. A genuine agent spends 42 only once.
